newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT says 1996 local revenues up sharply.
newsitem.headline: PLDT says 1996 local revenues up sharply.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) said on Wednesday its local network revenues and income from national long-distance calls contributed significantly to a 12 percent increase in net profit in 1996.
The telecommunications giant earlier reported 1996 net profit at 6.44 billion pesos against 5.751 billion in 1995.

PLDT said in a statement that local network revenues rose 25.8 percent in the year, primarily due to an increase in the number of telephone lines to about 1.52 million at the end of 1996 from 1.12 million at the end of 1995.
It said also that national long-distance revenues rose by 27.7 percent as a result of increasing call volumes.

International long-distance revenues increased by only 5.2 percent reflecting the combined effect of an increase in volumes, the weakening of the peso against the dollar and a continuing decline in accounting rates, it said.
Overall revenues rose 13.3 percent to 28.616 billion pesos in 1996, PLDT said.

Operating expenses increased by 2.4 percent in the year to 17.247 billion pesos due to higher depreciation charges and increased employee benefits, it said. Other expenses increased by 38.5 percent to 9.56 billion pesos primarily due to a higher level of borrowing in 1996, it said.
